command: Planning-only benchmark case. Do not call tools. Analyze this Rust async bug in Eli. A gateway owns JoinSet workers. On shutdown it calls abort_all(), then immediately drops the JoinSet. Sometimes child tasks keep writing completion messages after shutdown, and tests flake because cleanup returns before JoinHandle cancellation is observed. Return strict JSON with keys root_cause, minimal_patch, tests. Mention how to keep function bodies small. No markdown.

cases.stdout_tail:
WARN ELI_FALLBACK_MODELS is not set — no fallback models configured; context overflow errors will not automatically retry on a smaller model
2026-05-18T14:07:49.967762Z  WARN auto-handoff: provider did not return usage, estimating input tokens from response char count estimated_tokens=327
{
  "root_cause": "JoinSet::abort_all() only enqueues cancellation signals; it does not wait for child tasks to observe them. Dropping the JoinSet immediately after abort_all() triggers its Drop impl, which polls outstanding tasks once, but does not block until all JoinHandles resolve. Tasks mid-write survive long enough to produce side effects after shutdown() returns, causing flaky tests.",
  "minimal_patch": "In the gateway's shutdown method, replace the abort_all()-then-drop sequence with: (1) call abort_all() to signal cancellation, (2) loop over join_next().await, collecting results until None, (3) only then drop the JoinSet. This guarantees every child observed cancellation and terminated before cleanup returns. Wrap the drain loop in a helper like async fn drain_joinset(js: &mut JoinSet<T>) to keep the shutdown function body under 10 lines.",
  "tests": "1. Spawn a worker that enters a tight non-yielding loop writing to a shared AtomicBool after the shutdown signal arrives; assert the AtomicBool is never true after shutdown() resolves. 2. Spawn a worker that sleeps inside a write and assert the write buffer is closed before shutdown() returns. 3. Stress-test: spawn 100 workers, race shutdown against completion writes, assert no messages leak after shutdown over 1000 iterations."
}
